title: Common-stage inclusion preserves the proper projection factor
statement: Fix D,C,H:SixFunctorCommonStages(D,C), a finite coefficient field E and a compactified square Q [def-sf-operation-stages]. Use the canonical natural tensorator t of [def-sf-common-projection-tensor-comparison] and the factor maps and middle comparison of [def-sf-projection-mate-factors]. For every rational K on Q.X and N on Q.Y at E, the following square commutes: i_Y(properFactor_E);middle = source;properFactor_common. Here the common factor is evaluated on i_X K and i_Y N; source and target are the prescribed endpoint comparisons of [lem-sf-rational-projection-tensor-compatibility]. This is only the proper factor of the argument, and makes no assertion about the other factor or invertibility of the whole projection. The canonical tensor/pullback comparisons are those of [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison].

source.place: Compatibility and the common finite coefficient-field paragraph: flat extension of scalars respects the units, counits, associativity and specified projection mate.

proof.text: Transport the supplied tensor/pullback comparison and adjunction into the named operation coordinates. The equality transports in properFactor then cancel, leaving tensor of the normalized support identification followed by the right-adjoint projection mate. Expand sixFunctorFactoredSupportIdentification. The coefficient composition, openIdentification and properIdentity equations, with naturality of the proper identification and support comparison, prove its compatibility with the composite of the open-extension and direct-image comparisons.

Use the canonical tensor/pullback compatibility on every pair of rational inputs. The coefficient counit equation identifies the given direct-image comparison with the mate of the inverse pullback comparison. Apply the proved general map_rightAdjointProjectionMap_comp_mateEquiv theorem to obtain the proper projection square at the open-extended object. Naturality of this proper mate in that object carries the open-extension comparison. Finally use naturality of the canonical tensorator and the support-identification square to identify the source with source and the target with middle. This proves the displayed properFactor square; no open projection map or invertibility assumption is used.

lean.statement:
theorem commonProjectionProperFactor
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    (H : SixFunctorCommonStages D C) (E : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields C.l C.Qbar)
    (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
    (K : GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Stage C.l C.Qbar Q.X.obj.left E)
    (N : GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Stage C.l C.Qbar Q.Y.obj.left E) :
    (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
        (l := C.l) (Ω := C.Qbar) (Y := Q.Y.obj.left) E).map
        (properFactor ((H.coefficientStages E).rationalExchange Q) K N) ≫
        (middle (H.commonStageComparison E) (commonProjectionTensorComparison H E)
          Q K N).hom =
        (source (H.commonStageComparison E) (commonProjectionTensorComparison H E)
          Q.f Q.compactification K N).hom ≫
        properFactor (H.commonStageExchange Q)
          ((GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
            (l := C.l) (Ω := C.Qbar) (Y := Q.X.obj.left) E).obj K)
          ((GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion
            (l := C.l) (Ω := C.Qbar) (Y := Q.Y.obj.left) E).obj N)
